messages:
Alex Li: heads up — customer on Dedicated seeing embedding dim flip after model rollout. their app expects 1024 but responses are 1536 now. high priority, they're rate-limited by downstream indexer.
Sara G: ugh. do we have request id / example? can you paste the raw request + response body (no PII) and SDK/lang used?
Alex Li: paste below. they call embeddings via our TS SDK from a worker. request ts=2026-03-12T14:02:03Z request_id=rid_9f3a
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"embedding-1024","input":["foo","bar"],"batch_size":16}'
response snippet: {"data":[{"embedding":[...1536 numbers...],"index":0},{"embedding":[...1536 numbers...],"index":1}],"model":"embedding-1536-v2","usage":{}}
Sara G: interesting — request specifies embedding-1024 but response model is embedding-1536-v2. that suggests routing to an incompatible model variant. are they using routing policies / fallback?
Sam W: pinging infra to see if a canary with 1536 slipped into the 1024 alias. @ingest-bot can you check alias mapping and recent deploys?
ingest-bot: alias-check: alias "embedding-1024" currently points to engine-id: eng-42 (embedding-1024-v1) as of 2026-03-10T20:11:02Z. recent deploys: eng-53 (embedding-1536-v2) deployed to us-west-2 canary group at 2026-03-12T13:55:12Z. No automatic alias swap recorded.
Maria P: customer also mentioned intermittent empty vectors when using batching. could be an SDK batching + reorder bug where responses from different model variants get interleaved. any chance the router returned mixed-model shards?
Alex Li: empty vectors occur ~1/200 requests. repro steps I ran locally with TS SDK v1.3.8:
```ts
const client = new Redwood({ key: process.env.RW });
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'embedding-1024', input: bigArray, batch_size: 32, timeout: 30000 });
```
Sometimes entries in the returned array are [] or all zeros. No 500s. header x-request-id present.
Sara G: which TS SDK version? we shipped a patch last week for batch ordering but only for v1.4.x. v1.3.8 had a known issue where parallel batch responses could be merged if preserve_order flag not set.
Sam W: we also had a router change that multiplexes short/long sequences to different model variants for cost optimization. bug: when fallback occurs mid-batch, response dims could mismatch if model variants have different dims. this is on us. tracking as ENG-1129.
Alex Li: customer hit production with 4 nodes indexing parallel. they're throttling us for bad vectors. they want immediate mitigation (pin model, disable batching, patch SDK).
Maria P: immediate mitigations: 1) ask customer to pin exact engine id (not alias) — e.g., engine: "eng-42" in API call; 2) set batch_size:1 or disable batching in SDK; 3) upgrade TS SDK to v1.4.3 which adds preserve_order=true and dims check; 4) add client-side verification of vector length and retry on mismatch with exponential backoff.
Alex Li: can we provide sample code snippet for the customer to add a quick guard?
Sara G: yes — here's a minimal JS guard they can add while we fix server routing:
```ts
async function safeEmbed(client, input){
  const resp = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'eng-42', input, batch_size: 1, timeout: 15000 });
  if(!resp.data || !resp.data.every(d=>Array.isArray(d.embedding) && d.embedding.length === 1024)) {
    // log + retry once with jitter
    await wait(200 + Math.random()*400);
    return client.embeddings.create({ model: 'eng-42', input, batch_size: 1, timeout: 15000 });
  }
  return resp;
}
```
Alex Li: thanks. customer asks for a server-side fix timeline — any ETA to stop routing 1024 alias to 1536 canary?
Sam W: infra rollback started — removing eng-53 from canary group now. ETA ~20m. also adding a server-side validation: if a model alias expects 1024 and we detect a 1536 variant, router will not accept it for that alias and will fail the canary promotion. will be in patch release in ~2 hours.
Maria P: also notify support to watch for retry storms if customers implement client-side retries. recommend backoff and capping concurrency.
Alex Li: customer tried Go SDK too and saw timeouts during retries — they used default 5s per request. they increased to 20s and reduced concurrency, which helped. do we have recommended SDK timeout/backoff settings?
Sara G: doc suggestion: for batch workloads with large indexers: timeout >= 20s, max_concurrency 4 (per worker), use exponential backoff starting 200ms, cap retries at 3. We'll add to KB.
Sam W: quick root cause summary for ticket: 1) Canaried embedding-1536-v2 into infra that also serves embedding-1024 alias; 2) router multiplexed batches across variants for perf; 3) TS SDK v1.3.8 lacked preserve_order/dim-check causing intermittent empty or wrong-dim vectors; 4) customer-side concurrency + short timeouts amplified failures.
Alex Li: great. I'll send workaround steps to the customer (pin engine, upgrade SDK or set batch_size:1, guard vector length, widen timeouts). keep me posted on rollback.
ingest-bot: rollback complete: eng-53 removed from canary group at 2026-03-12T14:20:09Z.
Sam W: rollback done, routing fixed. I'll keep ENG-1129 open until patch released.
Maria P: follow-up: I'll add KB article and sample snippets for Python/Go/TS with recommended timeouts/backoff and a small validator function.
Alex Li: thanks team :thumbsup: customer says initial tests look good after pinning eng-42 and upgrading SDK. closing for now, will reopen if they see more anomalies.
support-bot: ticket updated: #CUST-8921 -> status: awaiting-customer-confirmation -> assigned: Alex Li
Maria P: note for postmortem: add automated canary validation to verify embedding dim compatibility when promoting variants.
Alex Li: noted. saving logs and request_ids to the ticket.
